NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner (CEC) and election commissioners (ECs) should be heard by a five-judge Bench.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and sought its listing. “We will examine and take a call,” the CJI said.The split verdict was delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. Justice Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge and opposed referring it to a larger Bench, while Justice Sharma favoured a five-judge Bench.With the two judges differing on the issue, the matter was referred to the CJI for constitution of an appropriate Bench.The top court's agreement came a day after massive protest by Rahul Gandhi-led opposition demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over poll body's special intensive revision exercise.

The split verdict was delivered by justices dipankar datta and satish chandra sharma. Article Title: Travis and Jason Kelce quietly donated $10,000 to help turn a $50,000 Olympic fundraiser into a family reunion in Milan
Article Text:
Travis and Jason Kelce (Instagram)

Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce helped Laila Edwards’ family reach Milan

Travis Kelce supported Laila Edwards before Olympic gold

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis and Jason Kelce made a quiet contribution that helped make a special Olympic moment possible for U.S. hockey star Laila Edwards. The brothers donated $10,000 to a fundraiser that helped bring Edwards’ family and friends to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics. Their support came after her family faced a difficult choice between watching her Olympic debut and covering everyday household expenses. Edwards went on to help Team USA win gold, creating a moment her family could celebrate together.Edwards’ Olympic journey was already historic before she stepped onto the ice. The 22-year-old became the first Black American to win an Olympic medal in women’s ice hockey after Team USA defeated Canada in the gold-medal game.But getting her loved ones to Italy was not easy.Edwards’ father, Robert Edwards, launched a GoFundMe campaign titled “Send Laila’s Family to the Olympics to Cheer Her On!” with a $50,000 target. The goal was designed to help the family avoid choosing between Olympic travel and essential bills at home in Cleveland Heights, Ohio.The Kelce brothers, who also grew up in Cleveland Heights, had followed Edwards’ career since she became the first Black player to make the U.S.senior women’s national team in 2023. They later supported her through an anonymous $10,000 donation.The contribution helped make the trip possible for 14 people, including Edwards’ parents, grandmother, aunt, cousin and older brother.The family had initially been able to afford travel for only two people.“We had to start talking about how to get money,” her mother Charone Gray-Edwards said, according to the Associated Press. “Who would go? How would we afford it?”The Chiefs tight end’s support extended beyond the financial contribution. Travis also reached out to Edwards before her Olympic debut, offering encouragement as she prepared for the biggest stage of her young career.“He was just saying, everyone’s got my back. He’s rooting for me,” she said, per the AP. “They didn’t have to do that, but they did. And I’m really grateful.”Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie, were also in the stands for the gold-medal game, giving Edwards a familiar connection to her hometown while she represented the United States.Edwards made an impact on the ice, recording an assist during the gold-medal victory. Team USA eventually defeated Canada 2-1 in overtime, securing only the third Olympic gold medal in U.S. women’s hockey history.For Edwards, the victory was more than a sporting achievement. Her family had made the long journey to Milan, and the Kelce brothers had quietly helped make that possible. Their involvement added another meaningful layer to an already historic Olympic chapter.
Article Summary: Travis and jason kelce donated $10,000 to a fundraiser that helped bring laila edwards' family and friends to milan for the 2026 winter olympics. Edwards went on to help team usa win gold, creating a moment her family could celebrate together.

Article Title: “Not have been able to go without his help”: How Conor McGregor turned from a hero into a helping hand for two 13-year-old fans with a €10,000 heartwarming move
Article Text:
How Conor McGregor turned from a hero into a helping hand for two 13-year-old fans(Getty Images)

Conor McGregor gave the twins €10,000 when they needed it most

The €10,000 gift became bigger than one trip

For Adam and Dylan Duffy, Conor McGregor had always been the fighter they looked up to. The Ballycanew twins had started their own MMA journey and dreamed of competing on a bigger stage. Then, in June 2022, McGregor noticed their fundraiser and stepped in with €10,000. The donation did more than help two young fighters reach Abu Dhabi. It gave them a moment they never expected from the man they had followed for years.Adam and Dylan had earned places on the Irish MMA Youth International Team and were preparing for the IMMAF Youth World Championships in Abu Dhabi in 2022. But getting there came with a cost. The twins launched a fundraiser with a target of around €6,000 to cover their trip.Their mother, Liz Duffy, also tried to spread the word online. She tagged McGregor in social media posts and hoped he might share the boys' story. Instead, the former UFC champion did something much bigger.In June 2022, McGregor donated €10,000 to the fundraiser. He then commented online: “Done! Do the land proud I know.” The donation pushed the twins beyond their original target and gave them the financial support they needed for the trip.The reaction from Adam showed just how much the moment meant to them. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022 after learning about the donation, Adam said he was at training when his coach told him about it.Surprisingly, Adam initially thought his coach was joking until he saw McGregor’s comment himself. He even joked that he now felt he had to win because McGregor had donated the money.“I was going insane!I thought he was joking until he showed me the comments. I feel like I have to win now because he donated all that money.’ Adam said.Dylan also understood how important the donation could be. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022, he said the brothers might not have been able to make the trip without McGregor’s help.He said, “We might not have been able to go without his help. There are so many gyms out there and he donated to us, which is insane.”That made the gesture more personal. The twins had spent years watching McGregor compete. Now, the UFC star had helped them take the next step in their own MMA careers.The twins did not stop fundraising after McGregor's donation. Adam and Dylan, along with their parents Jason and Liz, planned to use extra funds to buy equipment for their coach Richie Ivory’s gym and help other Irish fighters travel to the IMMAF World Championships. They also planned to support the Waterford Neonatal Unit, where the twins were born.The brothers had already spent four years training with Ivory before the 2022 championship opportunity. They first joined his jiu-jitsu classes after he returned to Ireland from Australia. Their training later moved toward MMA, where both boys developed a strong interest in the sport.McGregor’s €10,000 donation therefore did not simply cover a plane ticket. It helped two young Irish fighters chase a dream they had worked toward for years.For Adam and Dylan, there was also a personal reward. After receiving the donation, they hoped to meet McGregor at his pub and thank him themselves. Adam even joked, “I’m basically friends with Conor now!"For two 13-year-old fighters who had grown up admiring McGregor, getting help from their hero was already an unforgettable chapter. The fact that his €10,000 gift could also help other young Irish fighters made the story even bigger.
Article Summary: Adam and dylan duffy had earned places on the irish mma youth international team. They were preparing for the immaf youth world championships in abu dhabi in 2022. The twins launched a fundraiser with a target of around €6,000 to cover their trip. Conor mcgregor noticed their fundraiser and stepped in with €10,000.

Article Title: Lionel Messi's emotional farewell ends in one goal, two assists and a 3-0 win for Argentina over Benin
Article Text:
Lionel Messi (Reuters Photo)

Messi's assist prompts opener

Messi on the scoresheet

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi ’s final appearance for Argentina ended with victory, emotion and one last unforgettable night at the Monumental as the South American side defeated Benin 3-0 on Wednesday.The occasion was as much about Messi as the result. The stadium was packed long before kick-off, with the Argentine captain receiving an extraordinary farewell.Fabio Santana, a Malvinas War veteran and singer, performed the Argentine national anthem as Messi stood alongside his children, visibly emotional. A giant Messi shirt covered the pitch before the crowd erupted into a rendition of “Muchachos”.At the 10-minute mark, the match paused for another tribute, with every Benin player taking the opportunity to shake Messi’s hand.Argentina dominated possession early and repeatedly tried to find their captain in dangerous positions. Messi came close with a free-kick from outside the box, but Benin’s goalkeeper made a fine save.Lautaro Martínez also threatened after a run into the area, while another Messi pass nearly released him into space. Benin, however, refused to sit back completely and gradually grew into the contest.They eventually switched to a back five, with Messi receiving close attention whenever he came near the penalty area.As it happened: Argentina vs Benin Highlights The breakthrough finally arrived shortly after half-time. Julián Álvarez won a corner after bursting down the left, and Messi delivered the set-piece perfectly.Nicolás Otamendi, left completely unmarked, volleyed home to put Argentina ahead. It was a fitting goal for the veteran defender, who was also making his final appearance for the national team.Argentina doubled their advantage through Nico Paz. The youngster, who had just come onto the pitch as a substitute, collected the ball and produced a beautiful left-footed curling finish, drawing comparisons with Messi’s trademark style.Messi was involved again, providing the assist as Paz announced himself on the biggest stage.Then came the moment everyone inside the Monumental had been waiting for. Messi stepped up from the penalty spot and calmly sent the goalkeeper the wrong way, placing the ball into the top-right corner for 3-0.There was still time for one final glimpse of magic. Messi had a late effort saved before another strike hit the post, and in the dying seconds he won a free-kick in his familiar range. He took responsibility one last time, but the effort sailed over the crossbar.The whistle confirmed Argentina’s 3-0 victory. For Messi, though, the scoreline was almost secondary. The night belonged to the boy from Rosario who became Argentina’s greatest footballer, and who finally said goodbye to the shirt he made his own.
Article Summary: Argentina defeated benin 3-0 in lionel messi's final appearance for the national team. Messi was given an emotional farewell before kick-off at the monumental in new delhi. Julián álvarez, nicolás otamendi and nico paz all scored for argentina.

NEW DELHI: Captain Shreyas Iyer created a new record for India in T20I cricket after scoring a stunning unbeaten century against the West Indies in Lucknow on Tuesday evening. With the score, he surpassed one record held by legendary Virat Kohli.Batting at No. 4, the Indian captain smashed 102 not out from just 43 balls, hitting 10 fours and six sixes. His explosive innings helped India chase down 172 runs and win the first T20I by eight wickets.Iyer’s knock was his first T20I hundred and made him the first Indian captain to score a century while chasing in the format.The previous best belonged to Virat Kohli, who remained unbeaten on 94 from 50 balls against the West Indies in Hyderabad in 2019.Iyer also became only the third Indian captain to score a T20I century. Rohit Sharma had three centuries as captain, while Suryakumar Yadav also reached three figures against South Africa in December 2023.Despite Iyer’s record-breaking effort, he is still some distance behind the overall record for the highest score by a captain in a T20I chase.Pakistan’s Babar Azam remains at the top with 122 from 59 balls against South Africa in Centurion in 2021.Babar’s score was later matched by Singapore captain Aritra Dutta, who also made 122 against Japan in Bangkok in 2024.Iyer’s unbeaten 102 now sits seventh on the all-time list, but his remarkable strike rate of 237.2 makes the innings one of the most explosive captaincy knocks in T20I cricket.
Article Summary: Shreyas iyer breaks virat kohli's t20i captaincy record. Indian captain smashed 102 not out from just 43 balls, hitting 10 fours and six sixes. His explosive innings helped india chase down 172 runs and win the first t 20i by eight wickets.

Article Title: ‘History will be kinder to you’: Gautam Gambhir bids farewell to Ajit Agarkar
Article Text:

India head coach Gautam Gambhir bid farewell to outgoing chief selector Ajit Agarkar , praising his conviction and highlighting the three ICC trophies India won during his tenure.“Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you. Those 3 ICC trophies are testimony of your conviction: Team first & Team ahead, always.. I must say, History will be kinder to you. Thank you for everything. My heartfelt wishes for your future endeavours,” Gambhir posted on X.Agarkar’s tenure as chairman of the senior men’s selection committee officially ended on Tuesday, with the BCCI inviting applications to fill the vacant position.The former India pacer took charge in July 2023 and completed his term on October 4. He had informed the BCCI after its Annual General Meeting on September 18 that he would not seek an extension.During Agarkar’s stint, India reached the 2023 ODI World Cup final before winning the 2024 T20 World Cup, the 2025 Champions Trophy and the 2026 T20 World Cup.Gambhir, who worked closely with Agarkar during his tenure as India head coach, acknowledged the selector’s approach of putting the team ahead of individual considerations.Former India spinner Pragyan Ojha is currently serving as interim chairman of selectors and chaired the meeting that picked India’s squad for the upcoming New Zealand tour.Ojha, who played 24 Tests for India, could be appointed the full-time chairman based on seniority if the BCCI’s eventual choice has played fewer Tests.Parthiv Patel , whose name has emerged as a possible addition to the selection panel, would have greater seniority than Ojha, having played 25 Tests for India.The BCCI has invited applications for one position on the five-member senior men’s selection committee. Shiv Sundar Das, Ajay Ratra and RP Singh are the other current members.

Article Text:

The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi. Sujith Somasunder | Former India and Karnataka opener

NEW DELHI: One will have to feel for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Whenever VVS Laxman has been at the helm, Sooryavanshi has played for India, be it in Zimbabwe or at the recently concluded 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. To accommodate the teenager in the playing XI, Sanju Samson moved down to No. 3. But with Gautam Gambhir back for the West Indies T20I series, Sooryavanshi has been left warming the bench.The youngster did make his India debut under Gambhir during the tour of England earlier this year, but India's head coach made it clear that Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his opportunity. Gambhir has also made no secret of his faith in Samson, India's Player of the Tournament in the 2026 T20 World Cup. He admitted that leaving the Kerala batter out during India's tour of England was the "toughest decision" he has made since taking charge as head coach.In the first T20I against West Indies, Sooryavanshi was again on the bench, with Samson opening alongside Abhishek Sharma. Samson's stay at the crease lasted only nine balls before he hit a half-tracker straight back to Akeal Hosein. It was a soft dismissal, and in the commentary box, Ian Bishop, one of Samson's many admirers, could not help but question the batter's consistency.The question, then, is where does that leave Sooryavanshi?Sujith Somasunder, former India and Karnataka opener and a sports psychologist, believes the teenager now has to learn how to navigate a world that has changed dramatically since his emergence as one of Indian cricket 's biggest young stars.“Sooryavanshi has achieved what he has achieved so far on his own. Now, suddenly, his status in the cricketing world has moved to a different tangent. The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi. That is a very important aspect of how he will be able to control and manage this situation,” Somasunder told TimesofIndia.com.“Sooryavanshi has to realise that, ‘I am now going to get into the water, so I need to know how to swim.’ Similarly, he needs to understand that the world I am in now is a little different from what it was before I became Sooryavanshi. He will also need to learn and understand how to navigate this situation for himself,” he added.Sooryavanshi is now fighting for a place in the playing XI with Samson, the man whose 97 not out, 89 and 89 in the knockout stages helped India defend their T20 World Cup title. But since those heroics, Samson has managed only two half-centuries in 11 innings, both coming in Delhi, a venue traditionally favourable to batters. In six of those innings, he has been dismissed for single-digit scores.Sooryavanshi, meanwhile, is still only 15. He has already become a superstar, despite being at the very beginning of his international career. He endured a difficult start against Jofra Archer and Co. in England, but found his groove in Zimbabwe and looked in excellent touch at the Asian Games.Yet Gambhir has drawn a clear line for now. Unless Samson's lean run continues, Sooryavanshi could have to wait longer than expected for another opportunity.Gambhir, however, has stressed that Samson does not need anyone to validate his place in the team, pointing to his performances as proof of his ability.“First of all, he doesn't need to give me any credit (for proper communication when he wasn't playing). His talent itself is enough for him to be in the dressing room. He's shown what he's capable of. Someone doesn't become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having the talent. So he's done enough,” Gambhir said in an interview with Jio Hotstar, praising Samson.“From Vaibhav's point of view, it was again a very clear conversation that he has to wait for his opportunity. We know the kind of talent he has. We know what he can do,” Gambhir had said about Sooryavanshi.For Somasunder, though, the waiting period is not necessarily a setback. It could be an important part of Sooryavanshi's development, provided the teenager is given the right support and guidance.He gives the example of Australia and Ricky Ponting , a prodigiously talented youngster who was identified early as a potential future leader.“In the world of cricket, the way it has gone in India, the onus is always on the individual. In Australia, for example, I remember Ricky Ponting was a very brash young talent. I have heard, though I am not sure if it is true and I have not verified it, that the Australian Institute of Sport, as it was called initially, identified Ricky Ponting as a leader. What they did was take the initiative to groom Ponting as the next captain. He was a very brash young kid, but if they saw that he could be the future captain of the Australian team, then they needed to groom him to behave appropriately and develop the right leadership skills,” he said.Somasunder believes Indian cricket could similarly look beyond simply managing Sooryavanshi's performances and invest in preparing him for the pressures that come with being one of the country's most talked-about young cricketers.“Meanwhile, in our culture, which is relationship-oriented, Australia could be described as more task-oriented. So there are certain nuances to a relationship-oriented culture when it comes to individuals.In a task-oriented culture, there is more individualism. In a hierarchical culture, people tend to bow down to someone higher in the hierarchy. In an individualistic culture, everybody will call themselves by their own name and might even call the coach by his first name,” he added.For Sooryavanshi, this may be his first real lesson in the less glamorous side of international cricket. He has already learnt how to announce himself on the biggest stage. Now, he must learn how to wait for it. At 15, that patience could prove just as important as the talent that got him there in the first place.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi has been left on the bench for india's t20i series against west indies. The 15-year-old was named player of the tournament in the 2026 t20 world cup. Sujith somasunder, former india and karnataka opener and a sports psychologist, believes the teenager now has to learn how to navigate a world that has changed.

Article Title: 'Captaincy ends': Harmanpreet Kaur’s top five achievements as India captain
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Kaur

1. Leading India to its maiden Women’s ODI World Cup title

Harmanpreet Kaur with World Cup title

2. Leading India to back-to-back Asian Games gold medals

Nagoya: India's captain Harmanpreet Kaur, right, and Gunalan Kamalini pose for photographs with Gold medals after winning the women's final T20I cricket match between India and Sri Lanka in the ongoing Asian Games 2026, in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma)

3. Winning four Asia Cup titles

4. Dominating T20I cricket and setting historic leadership milestones

5. Leading India to a historic Test victory at Lord’s

Harmanpreet Kaur wants more Test matches after historic win at Lord's (Reuters Photo)

A legacy that goes beyond the numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur ’s decision to step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all three formats marks the end of one of the longest and most significant leadership eras in Indian women’s cricket.The 37-year-old, who led India’s T20I side for a decade after taking over in 2016, became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking charge across formats in 2023. On Tuesday, she announced that she was ready to move on from leadership and return to playing simply “for the love of the game”.“Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” Harmanpreet wrote in her farewell statement.Her tenure was defined by landmark victories, records and moments that helped shape the modern era of Indian women’s cricket.From finally winning the ODI World Cup to establishing herself among the most successful captains in T20I history, Harmanpreet leaves behind a remarkable leadership legacy.Here are the five biggest achievements of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy stint.The biggest achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was undoubtedly India’s historic triumph in the Women’s ODI World Cup in November 2025.For decades, an ODI World Cup title had remained one of the biggest missing pieces in Indian women’s cricket.India had come agonisingly close before, finishing runners-up in 2005 and 2017, but the trophy continued to elude the team.That changed under Harmanpreet.Leading India on home soil, she oversaw the campaign that finally delivered the country its first-ever Women’s ODI World Cup title. The achievement carried enormous significance not only for Harmanpreet personally but also for the growth and visibility of women’s cricket in India.The triumph represented the culmination of years of progress. India had developed into a consistent force in international cricket, producing a generation of players capable of competing with the world's best. Harmanpreet's leadership was central to that transition.Winning a World Cup as captain is the defining achievement of any international cricketer. For Harmanpreet, doing so with the Indian women's team made the moment even more significant.The title also ensured that her captaincy legacy would be remembered for more than individual records. She became the leader who helped India cross the final barrier and turn years of promise into a world championship.Another significant achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was leading India to gold medals at consecutive Asian Games, reinforcing the team’s dominance in the T20 format on the continental stage.India won the women’s cricket gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where cricket made its return to the Games after a long absence. Harmanpreet’s side emerged victorious in the T20 competition, securing India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s cricket.India then successfully defended its title at the 2026 Asian Games, once again finishing at the top of the women’s T20 competition. The back-to-back triumphs highlighted the consistency of the Indian team under Harmanpreet’s leadership and added another pair of major medals to her captaincy résumé.Winning one Asian Games gold was a landmark achievement. Repeating that success four years later demonstrated that India had established itself as the dominant force in the continental competition.Another defining feature of Harmanpreet's captaincy has been India's dominance in the continental game.Under her leadership, India secured four Asia Cup titles, in 2012, 2016, 2022 and 2026, giving Harmanpreet the distinction of being the Indian captain with the most Asia Cup triumphs.The Asia Cup has traditionally been an important tournament for women's cricket in the region, providing teams with an opportunity to test themselves against familiar opponents while also developing younger players.For India, success in the competition has reflected the team's sustained strength.Harmanpreet's four titles also demonstrate the longevity of her leadership. The fact that her successful campaigns stretched across more than a decade is particularly notable. Different teams, different opponents and different generations of Indian players came and went, but Harmanpreet remained a constant presence.The achievement saw her surpass Mithali Raj for the most Asia Cup titles by an Indian captain.That places Harmanpreet in distinguished company. Mithali was one of the central figures of Indian women's cricket for more than two decades, and succeeding her in the record books is a significant marker of Harmanpreet's own influence.The 2026 title was especially important because it came near the end of her captaincy tenure, providing another continental trophy to close one of the most successful leadership chapters in Indian women's cricket.Harmanpreet Kaur’s impact was perhaps most pronounced in T20I cricket, where she spent a decade at the helm after taking over as India’s captain in 2016. Her remarkable longevity not only made her one of the longest-serving leaders in women’s international cricket but also saw her establish several historic records.One of her biggest achievements came when she surpassed Australia’s Meg Lanning to become the captain with the most wins in women’s T20 internationals. The record reflects the consistency and longevity of Harmanpreet’s leadership at a time when the shortest format was undergoing rapid growth around the world.Her T20I tenure also produced another extraordinary milestone. Harmanpreet became the first cricketer in history to captain a side in 150 T20I matches, underlining the remarkable length of her leadership career.Reaching that landmark required far more than simply holding the captaincy. It reflected sustained selection, fitness, performance and, crucially, the confidence of teammates and coaches over many years. During her tenure, women's cricket witnessed the rise of franchise leagues, increasingly demanding international schedules and major tactical developments in T20 cricket.While Harmanpreet's greatest achievements have largely come in limited-overs cricket, one of her most memorable leadership moments arrived in the longest format.She guided India to a dominant 270-run victory over England at Lord's, in the first women's Test match played at the historic London venue.Lord's is one of the most iconic grounds in world cricket, and playing there carries enormous significance regardless of format. For the women's game, the occasion was historic in its own right.India's victory made the event even more memorable.A Test match places very different demands on a captain compared with T20 cricket. Leaders must manage sessions rather than individual overs, balance workloads across multiple days and constantly assess pitch conditions, field placements and bowling changes.Harmanpreet's ability to guide India to a comprehensive victory demonstrated her adaptability as a leader.The 270-run margin also highlighted India's superiority during the match. It was not merely a narrow escape or a hard-fought result; it was a commanding performance at one of cricket's most famous venues.For Harmanpreet, the achievement added another dimension to her captaincy record.Harmanpreet Kaur's decision to step down brings an era to a close, but her contribution to Indian women's cricket will extend far beyond captaincy statistics.She led India through a period of enormous change, from the rapid growth of T20 cricket to the expansion of women's franchise leagues and the eventual breakthrough of a World Cup triumph.Her five standout achievements, the 2025 ODI World Cup, the T20I captaincy wins record, four Asia Cup titles, the 150-match leadership milestone and the historic Lord's Test victory, encapsulate the scale of her tenure.Yet perhaps the most telling part of her farewell was her belief that the team is now “in a good place”.Harmanpreet is stepping away from the leadership role, but not from the game. As she put it, she is now ready to play for the love of cricket again.The captaincy may have ended. The journey, however, continues.
Article Summary: Harmanpreet kaur's decision to step down marks the end of one of the longest and most significant leadership eras in indian women's cricket. The 37-year-old led india’s t20i side for a decade after taking over in 2016. She became the odi captain in 2022 before taking charge across formats in 2023.

Article Text:

The Guardian

That Jeffrey Archer had a way with words would be an understatement. In 2019, the only year that he attended the Jaipur Literature Festival, he shared an anecdote that encapsulated the unique position he occupies among Indian readers of English.Archer recalled that a young urchin came up to him with pirated books and asked: “Sir, do you want the latest Jeffrey Archer?” To this, the author replied: “I am the latest Jeffrey Archer.”In that same interaction, he argued that RK Narayan should have won a Nobel Prize and congratulated the Indian team for beating the Aussies Down Under, which came after a session on stage that was filled to the rafters with about 8,000 people.Archer was a prolific writer and one who was more celebrated in India than in his native UK, where his public life often sullied his prowess as a scribe, though even legal misfortune would turn out to be a blessing in literary disguise as he churned out the utterly delightfulabout his time navigating Britain’s penal system.As thelede read: “…a best-selling British author, politician, philanthropist, athlete and one-time jailbird whose résumé seesawed between achievement and disgrace, and who inspired abiding public fascination with headline-grabbing accounts, both fictional and personal, of ambition, self-promotion, misbehaviour and scandal….”In his lifetime, he published 59 works, including 31 novels, 7 short-story collections and numerous other works. Archer’s later novels – perhaps the cut-off date is 2008 – would become a tad too reductive and formulaic. The good characters were, to borrow John Lennon’s lines, classless and free. The bad ones were usually class-conscious gits, and the women were very easily conned.Archer was the sort of writer who was very accessible to the aspirational post-liberalisation middle-class English reader who didn’t have the wherewithal to follow the trials and travails of a Holmes or a Smiley.His writing was more accessible, the vocabulary less grandiose and the literary style compelling without forcing one to grab a dictionary every single time.His last Instagram post hangs like a dangling modifier from the afterlife: “On Saturday 10th October at 7pm I will be discussing my final novel Adam & Eve….”Most great pieces of literary work, at least popular ones, are born out of some form of misfortune. Forsyth wroteupon facing penury after quitting the BBC and living on a friend’s sofa.Similarly, Archer wrotebecause, well, he was penniless and facing bankruptcy. But the real breakthrough came with, which sold as many copies asand. The latter, he recalled, was the “last great book” he read, in an interview with thein which he also admitted that he couldn’t get past page 30 ofand bragged with his usual braggadocio thatwas his “best novel”.also set the template of the Archer novel, with two Jungian ‘Archer-type’ (pun intended) protagonists who go head-to-head until one of them dies, after which comes a Bollywood-style twist.It was replicated in, which was a fictionalised version of the battle between media tycoons Rupert Murdoch and Robert Maxwell, with the latter ostensibly committing suicide in the end. In a cruel twist of fate, his daughter Ghislaine would be best known for her association with convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, who too shuffled off his mortal coil ostensibly of his own accord.’s follow-up,, has inspired many, including Angelica Aribam, founder of the Femme First Foundation and former NSUI General Secretary, who wrote on X that Archer’s plot piqued her interest in politics.Over the years, Archer would expand his genre to include art theft, Himalayan expeditions and CIA spy thrillers. His last major works were the, though one must confess one found them rather lacklustre compared to his earlier works.As X user Ritu Chaudhry wrote, his short stories, while not in the same league as the masters of that craft like HH Munro, Anton Chekhov, Isaac Asimov or Edgar Allan Poe – whose are, anyway? – were equally compelling, particularly because one could never guess the twist that came at the end.X user Wordita pointed out , Archer has a unique place among youngsters growing up in post-liberalisation India, along with Enid Blyton, Agatha Christie and John Grisham. One can add Sidney Sheldon to the list for those who were willing to risk their parents’ wrath if they were ever to scour through the pages. Also, as an aside, contrary to popular belief, Sidney Sheldon was born with the XY chromosome, not the XX one.Archer's life had the odd implausibility of an Archer novel. He entered Westminster as a Conservative MP at the age of 29 and seemed destined for a life in politics before losing everything in a fraudulent company, which prompted his first novel.In the 1980s, he was both a best-selling novelist and Margaret Thatcher’s deputy Conservative chairman before being laid low by a sex scandal and later winning damages. But the libel case would return, and an Old Bailey jury convicted him on several charges, which saw him spend two years in jail and became the basis for three bestselling prison diaries.And then he made another comeback, selling more than 300 million books, and remained in the House of Lords until retiring in 2024 and kept on working till the guy in the black robe came calling. His final novel,, was published on Oct 6, 2026 the day after he died.Sheridan Morley, one of his oldest friends, once described him as a man who will “dive over a cliff and then be amazed that he’s falling” because in his head, he’s “Peter Pan”.Morley recalled inin 2001, in a piece that described him as “mendacious, egotistical, ambitious, pushy, resilient, tactless, gullible, funny, charming, reckless, hard-working, generous, self-obsessed, loyal and naïve”, that he famously convinced the Beatles to support his Oxfam campaign and brought them to Oxford’s Brasenose College in 1964.That included bypassing their manager Bryan Epstein, and even the Beatles appeared flabbergasted at how they ended up under his charm.At the interval, Morley ran into Ringo Starr, the Beatles drummer, who asked if he knew who this Archer bloke was. Morley replied that everyone was trying to figure out who it was, to which the greatest drummer of all time replied: “He strikes me as a nice enough fella, but he’s the kind of bloke who would bottle your piss and sell it.”As far as epitaphs go, that’s perhaps the best description of the man who rewrote the bestseller charts, moved between Parliament and the peerage, survived financial ruin and tabloid scandal, went from the Old Bailey to Belmarsh, and still emerged to sell hundreds of millions of books around the world. Archer spent half a century writing about conmen, politicians, tycoons, rogues and impossible comebacks. In the end, none of his protagonists was quite as improbable, indefatigable or entertaining as Jeffrey Archer himself.
Article Summary: Archer was a prolific writer and one who was more celebrated in india than in his native uk. His writing was more accessible, the vocabulary less grandiose and the literary style compelling without forcing one to grab a dictionary every single time. Jeffrey archer died on october 6, 2026 - the day after his final novel was published.

Article Title: Exploring Florida nightclubs, spending time with cops, gang members and more: Here are the extraordinary lengths Rockstar’s research team went to develop GTA 6
Article Text:
Image via Rockstar Games

GTA 6 developers travelled across Florida for research

“Every game we make starts with research trips. It’s where to get to explore both the place and our ideas as a group,”

“To begin, a small group of us spent some time traveling from Miami through some of the surrounding towns and through the Florida Keys down to Key West. This is one of the best parts of the entire project: a car full of friends, driving for days on end, talking about what we want to make and being immersed in the locations and our ideas.”

Rockstar spent time with cops and gang members

“We do go in-depth, we hang with locals and we hear lots of stories and learn as much as we can. We travel around with cops and with gang members. Everyone is lovely. Some people are equally scary. We experience the underside as well; although the people who showed us around were among the nicest we’ve met, the stories, the places, the details could be terrifying. We try to build a world that is believable and varied, with depth, so that is the research we need,”

Developers explored Florida from the air

“I think we made the local news that day,”

Miami’s extremes will influence GTA 6

“Miami itself is really those extremes — lovely people, incredible wealth, incredible poverty, excess, craziness, the hustle, and showing it all off. That’s our research trips — experiencing those extremes so that we can bring them into our world, and it all finds its way into the game in surprising ways,”

Rockstar wants Leonida to feel believable

“the strange ways people react to events.”

Rockstar Games went far beyond conventional research while creating GTA 6’s fictional state of Leonida. The development team travelled across Florida, explored Miami and the Florida Keys , visited nightclubs and other locations, and spent time with people ranging from police officers and locals to gang members. The goal was to understand not just what Florida looks like, but also its people, culture, stories and the extremes that define the state.In an interview with Love, Rockstar Games Head of Development Aaron Garbut revealed that these research trips became an important part of the development process, with developers documenting everything from landscapes and local communities to the more unsettling side of Florida. The extensive research is expected to help Rockstar make Leonida feel more believable and detailed when GTA 6 arrives.GTA 6’s Leonida is heavily inspired by Florida, with Vice City serving as the game’s fictional take on Miami. Rockstar’s research team travelled across the state to understand the locations and culture that would eventually shape the game world.Speaking to Love Magazine, Garbut said the research trips typically begin with a small group scouting locations and exploring stories and ideas to incorporate into the game.Subsequent trips then involve more team members who spend additional time understanding the people, culture, and places.Garbut said.The research went beyond simply photographing buildings and landscapes. Rockstar developers reportedly spent time with locals, police officers and gang members to understand different sides of life in Florida.Garbut added.This approach could prove particularly relevant to GTA 6, which follows protagonists Jason and Lucia as they become involved in a criminal underworld in Leonida.Rockstar also used aerial research to capture parts of Florida that would be difficult to understand from the ground. Garbut said he carries a camera and phone during these trips to document what the team encounters. During one research trip, Rockstar developers reportedly flew low and fast over mangrove inlets in the Everglades before ending the day above a stadium hosting a live Beyoncé concert.Garbut noted. The research allowed Rockstar to capture details of Florida’s landscape that could influence how Leonida looks and feels in the game.For Rockstar, understanding Florida also meant experiencing Miami's contrasting sides and those of the surrounding areas.Garbut continued.These details aren't limited to major locations or missions. Rockstar said elements such as pedestrian conversations, radio programmes and advertisements can also be influenced by its research.The studio does not consider these elements secondary content, particularly because players are expected to spend hundreds of hours exploring GTA 6’s world.Rockstar has historically placed significant emphasis on creating detailed open worlds, and GTA 6 appears to continue that approach. Rather than treating the environment as a backdrop, the studio wants Leonida to feel like a living world with its own people, stories and culture.The company is also taking a deliberate approach to satire. Garbut said Rockstar avoids directly recreating viral real-world moments because GTA games take years to develop, meaning references to specific events can quickly become outdated.Instead, GTA 6 will focus its satire on modern culture, conspiracy theories and
Article Summary: Gta 6's leonida is heavily inspired by florida, with vice city serving as the game’s fictional take on miami. Rockstar games’ research team travelled across the state to understand the locations and culture that would eventually shape the game world. Developers spent time with locals, police officers and gang members to understand different sides of life in florida.

Project Aces has apologised for a recent Steam issue. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve players must install and launch the main game to access Ace Combat Zero: The Belkan War, which is included as a pre-order bonus. The arrangement has drawn criticism because Ace Combat 8 requires at least 150GB of free storage, while The Belkan War can be launched separately on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.Project Aces said it is reviewing player feedback and discussing possible alternatives with its platform partners. However, the developer cautioned that “At this time, we cannot guarantee that any changes will be made.” The team also clarified that any potential change to the Steam launch method would not mean Ace Combat Zero becomes available as a separate purchase.
